Analysis by Richard Cowan 

Almost every week, the wonderful folks who sold us the Iraq War because they are too incompetent or too lazy to question authority or too afraid of losing their overpaid jobs, breathlessly report on the “latest research” on marijuana. 

See 

Bush So Drunk He Couldn’t Remember Doing Coke, So Medical Marijuana Patients Are Driven to Suicide. There Are A Lot of Questions the “Liberal Media” Still Will Not Ask. and 

Annotated NORML Weekly News for February 7, 2008; NORML Responds to “Latest Research”. Cannabinoids Kill Cancer. Noting Obama’s Retreat. 

and 

The Latest Research: Are “Dope Smoking Teens Addicted by Early 20s” Or Is Regular Drinking In Teens “Protective Against Cannabis Dependence.” Or Does Cannabis Protect Against Alcoholism? You Decide. 

Consider that from the beginning, this website has been based on the premise that “bad journalism” is the best two-word explanation for cannabis prohibition. And I am constantly documenting this point – at least to my own satisfaction. 

From 1998 see 

Marijuana Prohibition, Media Criticism, Copyrights and the 8th and 9th Commandments.

and from 2002, especially 

Negligent Journalism: Reader Beware or A Right to Expect More? The Drug Czar Says He Is “Subject to the Scrutiny of the Press.” The Significance of the Ultimate Lies. Analysis by Richard Cowan 

Nonetheless, it would never occur to me to suggest that there should be some law to punish those in the media who violate the most basic tenets of Judeo-Christian civilization and popular democracy by bearing false witness against their neighbors. 

See 

Today Is "International Anti-Drug Day" – Really. And Top UN Nark Wants To Censor Internet. Anti-Prohibitionism Equated With Genocide. The Internet Community Needs To Wake Up! 

As a point in case, consider this excerpt from HealthDay News, "Although growing literature suggests that long-term marijuana use is associated with a wide range of adverse health consequences, many people believe it is relatively harmless and should be legalized, the researchers noted. 

"However, this study shows long-term, heavy cannabis use causes significant brain injury, memory loss, difficulties learning new information, and psychotic symptoms, such as delusions of persecution [paranoia], delusions of mind-reading, and bizarre social behaviors in even non-vulnerable users," said lead researcher Murat Yucel, from the ORYGEN Research Centre and the Neuropsychiatry Centre at the University of Melbourne.” (All emphasis added) 

My point has nothing to do with the validity of the research. I have no idea whether or not smoking 5 or more joints a day for 10 years or more shrinks the hippocampus and amygdala, etc. I have been smoking cannabis for more than 40 years and none of the body parts that I really care about has shrunk. As for my rationality, I must leave that to the readers to judge. 

My point is that both the “research” and the “reporting” here are inherently political – and therefore deceitful. The arguments against marijuana prohibition are no more based on the assumption that cannabis is harmless than the arguments against censorship are based on the assumption that such crappy reporting is harmless. 

See 

“Marijuana Isn’t Harmless.” Okay, But Why Isn’t It Sold Over the Counter? Or Would You Ban Something That Causes 300,000 ER Visits Every Year, And Kills A Child Every Month? (Trick Question) 

Now in fairness to the reporter, the article did say “relatively harmless,” but “relative” to what? 

Is it “relatively harmless” when compared to other illegal substances like meth?

See 

Marijuana Bigger Problem Than Meth? DEAland And The Bush Administration Have a Very Serious Walters Problem. We Couldn’t Make This Up! 

Or is it “relatively harmless” when compared with legal substances like alcohol and tobacco? 

See 

The Strategy of Comparing Risks of Cannabis and Alcohol. When an Old Argument Catches On. Analysis by Richard Cowan 

and 

British Lung Foundation Cons Media. Blaming Cannabis for Problems Caused By Prohibition. Tripping Over the Party Line. The Media Fell For It, As Usual, But UK Anti-Tobacco Group Does Not. 

By contrast, consider the report from May of last year, “Drinking Heavy Amounts of Alcohol Shrinks Your Brain ”. 

There was very little media coverage of this report, and I will wager than none of them raised the point that many people still think that drinking alcohol should be legal. Similarly, in November of last year, there was a report from New Zealand that said , “It is estimated 800,000 New Zealanders binge drink regularly placing them at high risk of alcohol related brain damage… It is not just binge drinking that's risky. A female consuming three standard drinks a day for eight to 10 years and a male having six drinks, could leave you with a hangover for life." 

Nowhere in the article was there a mention of alcohol prohibition. If there are real dangers in the long term use of large amounts of cannabis, then the information should be presented in a credible way so that people can make their own informed decisions about whether the pleasure they are getting is worth whatever the risks might be. We make decisions like that every day about food, drink, travel, etc., and weigh the relative risks. On the other hand, we almost never see any speculation on the risks of the prohibitionist police state. 

We never hear anyone ask if marijuana prohibition is “harmless.” If only freedom remains “controversial,” then we are already slaves. 

See 

Bush Should Have John – Comical Ali – Walters Explain The Iraq War, Then The Media Would Never Ask Any Embarrassing Questions. Doctrine Of Drug Czar Infallibility? Blame Canada, Again. 

and 

How Prohibitionism Corrupts the New York Times: “Educating” the Children with the Party Line, and Undermining Journalistic Integrity. Analysis by Richard Cowan.

and 

Reuters Madness and the Subordination of Journalism to Prohibitionist Propaganda. Conning CNN. Lies Lead to Wars, But Then, That Is Their Purpose. 

The great Austrian economist, Ludwig von Mises, wrote, "For if the majority of citizens is, in principle, conceded the right to impose its way of life upon a minority, it is impossible to stop at prohibitions against indulgence in alcohol, morphine, cocaine, and similar poisons. Why should not what is valid for these poisons be valid also for nicotine, caffeine, and the like? Why should not the state generally prescribe which foods may be indulged in and which must be avoided because they are injurious?....We see that as soon as we surrender the principle that the state should not interfere in any questions touching on the individual's mode of life, we end by regulating and restricting the latter down to the smallest detail. The personal freedom of the individual is abrogated. He becomes a slave of the community, bound to obey the dictates of the majority.” 

For Paul Armentano’s take on the "latest research" racket, see Smoking Pot All Day, Every Day Might Not Be Good For You
